subject: Clarify support commitments & maintenance carveouts - Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbanalytics.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@nimbanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on SLA language and maintenance carveouts

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form and the SLA schedule. Our engineering and procurement leads reviewed it and we have a few clarifying questions before we can sign: 

1) Uptime measurement: You define availability as "service healthy" per region, but we need to confirm whether the metric is applied at the regional endpoint level or at the global account level. Nimbanalytics requires per-region guarantees for latency-sensitive customers.

2) Maintenance windows: The current redline gives Redwood the ability to perform maintenance with 8 hours' notice, up to 6 hours per month. Can you confirm whether emergency maintenance outside that window will be excluded from credits, and whether planned maintenance can be scheduled to avoid our APAC business hours?

3) Service credits: The draft uses a monthly credit scale capped at 50% of monthly fees. For business-critical pipelines we need the ability to escalate to additional credits or a temporary rollback to previous SLA terms if repeated violations occur.

4) Response times: Your P1/P2 response windows are listed as "Initial response within 1 hour" — can you confirm whether that applies to business hours or 24/7? Our security/compliance folks will insist on 24/7 for P1.

Attached is a redline (OrderForm_v3) with marginal notes from our Ops lead. We are aiming to finalize the Order Form this week if possible. Can you please loop in legal and ops so we can close the items above?

Thanks,

Sarah Lin
Head of Infrastructure
Nimbanalytics

Attachments: Nimbanalytics_OrderForm_v3_comments.pdf (annotated)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbanalytics.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language and maintenance carveouts

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed notes and for the quick turnaround. Appreciate the annotated PDF.

Quick answers up front so you have context while we align internally:
- Uptime measurement: Redwood measures availability per logical region (e.g., us-west-2, eu-west-1) by default. We can include the per-region metric in the Order Form instead of a global aggregation.
- Maintenance windows: Planned maintenance can be scoped to avoid APAC business hours where operationally feasible; we'll propose a standing monthly window and an opt-out process for critical customers. Emergency maintenance (safety/security) is currently excluded from credits but we can add tighter definitions around "emergency" to limit ambiguity.
- Service credits: We can add a mechanism to escalate relief (additional credits or negotiated remedies) for repeat monthly breaches, subject to a defined remediation timeframe and cap.
- Response times: For P1 incidents we offer 24/7 initial responses; for P2 the standard is business-hours. We'll make the P1 24/7 language explicit.

I'll pull in legal and ops to propose concrete redline language. Lauren, Markus, Karthik — can you review Sarah's attached comments and propose edits to the Order Form and SLA table? Key asks from Nimbanalytics are per-region uptime, explicit 24/7 P1, clearer emergency maintenance carveouts, and an escalation pathway for repeated breaches.

Next steps: I'll consolidate our suggested redlines and send back a single PDF and a one-page summary table of proposed credit tiers and definitions by EOD. If Nimbanalytics is available, I'd like to set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the proposed wording.

Best,
Olga
Director, Account Management
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix.xlsx (draft credit tiers)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language and maintenance carveouts

Thanks for the ping, Olga. I reviewed Nimbanalytics' annotated Order Form and drafted suggested language below that legal is comfortable with — high level: tighten definitions, keep caps but introduce a limited remediation escalation path, and narrow emergency maintenance scope.

Proposed legal edits (summary):
- "Availability" definition: change to "Measured per region using region-specific successful request rate over the billing period; global availability for overall reporting only." This addresses per-region guarantees while avoiding dual-credit calculations.
- "Emergency Maintenance": define as "unplanned changes required to address an active security vulnerability, integrity issue, or critical system failure." Add requirement to provide a written incident summary within 72 hours when invoking emergency maintenance. Emergency maintenance remains excluded from credit calculation.
- "Service Credits Escalation": allow the customer, after two consecutive months of SLA breaches in the same metric, to request a remediation review. If the remediation plan is not met within 30 days, allow application of an additional one-time credit up to 20% of the monthly recurring fees, capped at 70% cumulative credits across the two months.
- "P1 Response": explicitly state "Initial triage and acknowledgement: 24/7; Target mitigation timeline subject to incident complexity and agreed runbook." Keep P2 as business-hours initial response.

Operational note for Markus: if we accept the per-region measurement, Ops needs to confirm monitoring windows and how partial-region degradations map to credit thresholds. Markus — can you confirm monitoring granularity and realistic maintenance scheduling constraints?

I'll convert the above into track-change redlines on the Order Form and SLA schedule. Once we have Ops confirmation, we can send the consolidated redline to Nimbanalytics and propose a 30-minute review call.

-Lauren
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbanalytics.com>, procurement@nimbanalytics.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA language and maintenance carveouts

Sarah — attaching our consolidated redline (Nimbanalytics_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and a short summary table (redwood_sla_matrix.xlsx) that maps availability buckets to credit tiers and defines triggers. Highlights of our position: 

- Per-region availability: accepted. The Order Form now lists per-region measurement methodology and a single region-level credit calculation.
- Maintenance: planned maintenance will be scoped to an agreed monthly window; Redwood will provide 8 hours' notice for planned events. Emergency maintenance remains excluded from credits, but we added a strict definition and require a 72-hour incident summary whenever invoked.
- Service credits & escalation: we accepted a limited escalation path — two consecutive monthly breaches trigger a remediation review; failure to remediate within 30 days may yield an additional one-time credit (up to 20% of MRR) subject to a cumulative cap.
- Response times: P1 = 24/7 initial triage; P2 = business hours. Detailed runbook to be attached to the SOW if Nimbanalytics requests.

Please review the attached redline and let us know if you'd like to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and include Ops and Legal. If you prefer, we can accept minor tweaks directly in the PDF and finalize by EOD Thursday.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Account Management
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nimbanalytics_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf, redwood_sla_matrix.xlsx
